claim.summary: Adapted-basis criterion: over S = k[x]/(x^n) (k a field), for a finite family Sigma of submodules of a finitely generated free S-module F, with C the colon modules (M : x^j), M in Sigma, 0 <= j <= n, and phi(A) = (A + xF)/xF, the following are equivalent: (a) Sigma has a common adapted basis (F = sum S e_i, each M = sum x^{a_i(M)} S e_i); (b) (i) phi preserves finite intersections of members of C and (ii) the phi(C) generate a distributive lattice of subspaces of F/xF; (c) C together with xF generates a distributive lattice of submodules. Graded version with homogeneous bases. Proof: classical adapted basis of F/xF for a distributive subspace family (proved in the entry), lifts into meets of colons by (i), graded pieces and colength; (a) => (c) since monomial modules form a product of chains. Only colons enter, not multiples; the two recorded counterexamples fail (i) and (ii) respectively; triple checks of generators do not decide (c).
